title: Does the walk-state staleness fix (bug #7) require a one-shot reconciler CLI sub
question: Does the walk-state staleness fix (bug #7) require a one-shot reconciler CLI subcommand for consumer repos that have v0.6.0 walk-state.json files with tasks stuck at state: "running" for tasks that are actually merged on disk, or is it acceptable to document that a fresh --reset is required before the first v0.6.1 walker invocation? The answer determines whether a new cloverleaf-cli subcommand must be shipped alongside the SKILL.md fix.
findings: There is exactly one v0.6.0 walk-state.json file in the wild: `.cloverleaf/runs/plan/CLV-26/walk-state.json`, containing all three tasks (CLV-27, CLV-28, CLV-29) stuck at `state: "running"` with `last_seq: 0` — never updated during the actual drain. The blast radius is therefore a single file in a single repo; no other consumer repos exist. The v0.6.1 SKILL.md step 4 (Resumability) already contains built-in reconciliation logic: on every walker invocation it iterates over tasks with `state === "running"`, checks whether the claw-drive session is still live, and if stopped-cleanly checks the on-disk task status — if merged, it updates walk-state to `state: "merged"`; if not, it resets to `pending`. This means a stale v0.6.0 file is self-healing on the first v0.6.1 invocation provided the claw-drive sessions are no longer live (they are not — sessions from 2026-04-25 are long gone). However, the downstream scheduling impact is non-trivial before that first reconciliation tick: `computeReadyTasks` in `dag-walker.ts` counts `running` entries against the `maxConcurrent` cap, so three stale `running` tasks with `max_concurrent: 3` would exhaust all concurrency slots and prevent any new tasks from ever being scheduled — the walker would immediately see 0 ready tasks and exit. The cost of a dedicated reconciler subcommand is meaningful: it would need to query `git log --oneline --merges main` to find the merge commit for each task branch, construct the full `merged` state shape (adding `merged_at` and `merge_commit` to the existing `session_id`), then call `walk-state-write`. The schema for `merged` entries requires all three fields; partial in-place updates are not supported by the current `walk-state-write` interface, which replaces the entire file. The step-4 reconciler in SKILL.md covers the same ground more robustly (it also resets non-merged stopped sessions to `pending`), so a separate CLI subcommand would be redundant once v0.6.1 ships. The only plan that has a stale file (CLV-26) is fully complete — all three tasks are merged on main — so there is no in-flight work that `--reset` would destroy; `--reset` is therefore safe to run.
recommendation: Do not ship a reconciler subcommand. Instead, add a one-line note to the v0.6.1 CHANGELOG and the SKILL.md `--reset` documentation: 'If upgrading from v0.6.0, run `/cloverleaf-run-plan <PLAN-ID> --reset` before the first v0.6.1 walker invocation on any plan that has a stale walk-state.json from a completed v0.6.0 run. The --reset flag deletes the walk-state file and restarts scheduling from scratch; it is safe to use when all tasks in the plan are already merged on main (the only known case in the wild is CLV-26).' This is justified because: (1) the blast radius is one file in one repo; (2) all stale entries belong to a fully-completed plan, so --reset loses nothing; (3) the v0.6.1 step-4 reconciler would self-heal the file anyway on first invocation if sessions were live, but the scheduling deadlock (stale running entries exhausting all concurrency slots) means the walker would exit immediately before reconciliation could help — making --reset the only reliable fix; and (4) a reconciler subcommand adds ~30-50 lines of git-log parsing and schema construction that duplicates the step-4 logic already in the SKILL.md, with no consumer outside this one edge case.
